rationale:
Evidence from iteration 0: every trial on all three development tracks ended off track (oval 20/20, s-bend 20/20, slalom 20/20). Progress was 0.23 on the oval, 0.11 on the s-bend and 0.07 on the slalom. Each run logged 2.0 line-loss events, and max_error was about 0.063 to 0.067 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. The robot therefore fails early, mostly through line loss followed by drift, not through slow progress. The evaluator's conditional rule applies: line_loss_events is above zero, so reduce base_speed, and keep kp.

Causes I can infer: (1) the sensors span only x = -0.02 to +0.02. A sensor's 12 mm footprint reaches the 12.5 mm tape half-width only within about 18.5 mm of the centre, so once the robot drifts to about 0.02 m the outer sensors see nothing and the sum of readings can fall below 0.05. (2) At base_speed 1.6 the robot cannot correct before it leaves that narrow window.

Changes: (a) base_speed 1.6 to 1.3, which the evaluator's rule supports and which gives the robot more time to react. (b) Widen the sensor spread to x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 (15 mm spacing) so the line stays visible at larger offsets. Weights stay (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1), so the signal remains bounded by 1. (c) kp 4.0 to 5.0 for stronger correction at the wider sensor spacing, since the signal now changes more gradually. (d) kd 0.3 to 0.5 to damp the extra overshoot that a higher kp introduces. ki stays 0.05. line_loss stays last_direction.

Expected result: fewer line-loss events (target 0 or 1 per run), max_error below 0.05 m, and completion on the oval and s-bend. Progress may fall a little on the slalom because of the lower speed. Hypotheses to test: (H1) the line-loss events come from the sensors losing the tape at large offsets, so wider spacing should cut them. (H2) base_speed 1.3 is safe enough to finish. If the robot still runs off with zero line loss, kp is too low and should rise to about 6.0. If it finishes but takes more than 3 s, raise base_speed toward 1.5 once line loss is zero.
